_meta.source: Illustrative marginal-cost component breakdown for one gas-CC generator at one hour.
_meta.description: Shows how marginal cost assembles from heat rate, fuel price, emissions, NOx, carbon, minus EAC credits. One example: F-class gas-CC in ERCOT, July 2026.

price_environment.description: Mid scenario, forward case 2026. Henry Hub per HENRY_HUB_TRAJECTORIES['mid']. ERCOT Waha basis -0.50 per GAS_BASIS_DIFFERENTIAL. Carbon: RFF mid path.

components.source: NOX_RATES['gas_cc'] × assumed regional NOx allowance price
Gas-CC SO2 rate negligible; SO2 price from CAIR/CAVP allowance markets
policy/ira.py, model_year=2026, PTC applies to gas-CC post-2022 if emissions < 0.4 tCO2e/kWh
components.notes: Gas-CC with CCS or near zero carbon qualifies; base unit shown here does NOT qualify (0.38 > 0.4 cutoff is close). Illustrative: assume borderline retrofit scenario earns partial credit ~$13/MWh.

summary.description: Marginal cost $14.33/MWh. Hour clears at $65.2/MWh LMP (gas-CT is marginal). This unit is inframarginal; it dispatches in the economic ramp because its cost is well below the clearing price.

scenario_high_gas.notes: High gas path: dispatch may be out-of-merit by evening if gas spikes.

scenario_high_carbon.notes: High carbon path (RFF high): carbon cost dominates. Coal retires faster; gas-CC faces tougher competition from wind/solar + storage.
